_source: Placement library (4/N). Named-yoga callouts keyed by slug. Lets a kundli reading name and explain a detected yoga from the KB rather than asking the LLM to recall classical definitions (a known hallucination surface). Payload { name, text }. English-authored; run `npm run kb:backfill -- --tables=yoga-meaning`.

en.name: Gajakesari Yoga
en.text: Jupiter in a kendra (1/4/7/10) from the Moon. Confers intelligence, good judgement and lasting reputation; the native tends to be respected rather than merely popular.

en.name: Budhaditya Yoga
en.text: Sun and Mercury conjunct. Sharp analytical intelligence and clear communication. Strong when Mercury is not combust; when it is, the intellect is there but expression struggles.

en.name: Chandra-Mangala Yoga
en.text: Moon conjunct Mars. Drive fused with emotion — capable of real earning power, but the temper needs governing.

en.name: Ruchaka Yoga
en.text: Mars in own or exalted sign in a kendra. One of the five Mahapurusha yogas: courage, physical strength, command.

en.name: Bhadra Yoga
en.text: Mercury in own or exalted sign in a kendra. Mahapurusha yoga of intellect, eloquence and business acumen.

en.name: Hamsa Yoga
en.text: Jupiter in own or exalted sign in a kendra. Mahapurusha yoga of wisdom, ethics and a naturally teaching disposition.

en.name: Malavya Yoga
en.text: Venus in own or exalted sign in a kendra. Mahapurusha yoga of beauty, comfort, artistry and refined taste.

en.name: Sasa Yoga
en.text: Saturn in own or exalted sign in a kendra. Mahapurusha yoga of endurance, authority over others and slow, durable rise.

en.name: Dhana Yoga
en.text: A wealth combination formed when the lords of the 2nd, 5th, 9th or 11th connect. Indicates accumulation rather than windfall — money that stays.

en.name: Raja Yoga
en.text: A kendra lord linked with a trikona lord. The classical power combination: authority, status and material success together.

en.name: Viparita Raja Yoga
en.text: Lords of the 6th, 8th or 12th connecting among themselves. Rise THROUGH difficulty — setbacks that end up creating the opportunity.

en.name: Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga
en.text: A debilitated planet whose debilitation is cancelled. Often the most interesting placement in a chart: an early weakness that becomes a defining strength.

en.name: Kemadruma Yoga
en.text: No planet in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon. Traditionally a yoga of isolation and fluctuating support; substantially reduced when the Moon is aspected or in a kendra from the lagna.

en.name: Shakata Yoga
en.text: Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter. Fortunes that rise and fall in cycles rather than climbing steadily.

en.name: Amala Yoga
en.text: A benefic in the 10th from the lagna or Moon. Spotless reputation — the native's public name outlives their tenure.

en.name: Saraswati Yoga
en.text: Jupiter, Venus and Mercury well placed in kendras/trikonas or the 2nd. Exceptional aptitude for learning, art and expression.

en.name: Parivartana Yoga
en.text: Two house lords exchanging signs. Fuses the affairs of both houses — each is accessed through the other.

en.name: Kala Sarpa Yoga
en.text: All seven planets hemmed between Rahu and Ketu. Intense, karmically driven life with concentrated periods of pressure and breakthrough; effects soften markedly when a planet sits outside the axis.

en.name: Guru-Chandala Yoga
en.text: Jupiter conjunct Rahu. Unconventional wisdom that questions inherited belief — brilliant or misdirected depending on Jupiter's strength.

en.name: Adhi Yoga
en.text: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon. Confers leadership, resources and a comfortable, well-supported life.
